extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from source figures, methods, and supplementary Table S16; computational docking is not promoted to stand-alone direct proof.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: FFN self-assembles as nanoparticles and undergoes LPS/LTA-triggered conversion toward nanofibers; this is a direct assembly and microscopy-supported mechanism context rather than receptor-specific target proof.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Supports bacteria-triggered assembly behavior; does not alone prove bactericidal target specificity.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: N6 and FFN damage bacterial membrane morphology and permeability in tested E. coli and S. aureus strains.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct membrane phenotype evidence; exact molecular pore model is not assigned.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: FFN nanofibers physically capture or aggregate bacteria in microscopy and trapped-bacteria assays, complementing membrane disruption.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Capture evidence is phenotype-level and should not be generalized to all bacteria outside the tested strains.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Molecular docking models propose FFN interactions with LPS/LTA through hydrogen bonds and salt bridges, but this remains computational support for the direct LPS/LTA assembly observations.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Docking is not treated as direct mechanism proof without the microscopy and assembly assays.

caution_findings.evidence_context: Direct claims are limited to membrane damage, assembly transformation, and capture phenotypes in tested strains; docking remains computational support.
